scene.note: The tablet downloads a passenger list from a busy harbour server, tries again with growing waits when it is worth it, and stops everything the moment Odile cancels.

steps.note: The tablet wants the passenger list for S1. retry() calls the task with attempt 1.
The server is busy. The error is marked retryable, so it is worth another try.

value.label: the wait before each new try

steps.note: Before trying again it sleeps, and each wait is twice the one before, so the server is not hammered.
When an attempt works, retry resolves with its value and waits no more.
An error that is not retryable, like a sailing that does not exist, rejects at once. After the last attempt the last error comes back, with no final wait.
retry asks sleep() to wait 150 ms. If the signal it was given has already aborted, it rejects at once and starts no timer.
Otherwise it starts one timer and listens for the signal's abort event.
If Odile cancels first, the timer is cleared so it never fires, and the sleep rejects with the signal's reason.
If the timer fires first, the sleep resolves and removes its abort listener, because one signal outlives many sleeps.
Odile starts the S2 download with a signal she can abort when the sailing is called off for weather.
retry passes the signal on to every attempt and every sleep, so both can stop early.
Aborting cannot reach inside a running promise. retry looks at the signal each time it gets control back: before an attempt, when one fails, and after a wait.
An attempt that was already running may still fail with a retryable error after the abort. That is no reason to wait and try again.
Once the signal has aborted, nothing new starts, and the download rejects with the signal's reason. A signal that is already aborted never calls the task at all.
